label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Yellow sofa, left pillow, dark coffee table, two tea settings, flowers, rear wall and right curtain clearly reconstruct the scene identity.
Table remains in front of the sofa, flowers between the cups, pillow on the left and curtain behind the right end. Frontal framing simplifies the reference perspective.
Furniture and tabletop objects have broadly compatible relative sizes. Sofa depth is compressed and its base unusually tall, but functions remain recognizable.
Warm yellow upholstery, dark table and pot, white cups, green foliage and gray curtain preserve the main color organization despite simplified surfaces.
All principal objects are legible with coherent soft shadows. Lighting is flatter and less strongly right-directed than the reference, without obscuring content.
Complementary side and detail views reveal furniture thickness, cup volumes and spatial separation, establishing genuine three-dimensional construction.

Actual hierarchy links locate sofa, table, tea settings and plant meshes. Box.013, Box.037, Rod.085, Rod.092 and Rod.098 are nonempty MESH objects with material slots; their assigned materials have connected surface shaders.

dimension_scores.evidence: Main composition is readily recognizable, but blocky upholstery, sparse flowers and rigid curtain folds lose much of the reference character.
Furniture and tabletop objects appear supported. Rigid pillow construction and cup tops with little apparent cavity reduce physical credibility.
Major colors correspond, but the sofa is paler and flatter; curtain, cups and flowers have conspicuously simplified silhouettes.
Visible sampling noise, geometric fabric forms and sparse repetitive foliage give an early blockout appearance.
Principal front/back and left/right relationships are preserved, with a plausible gap between sofa and table.
Table and accessories are plausibly sized, but the sofa has shallow seating, thin back cushions and a disproportionately tall lower base.
Soft illumination maintains visibility, but weak directional contrast and uniform surface response poorly convey upholstery, wood and ceramic differences.
All principal furniture and accessory counts are present, including two cups and saucers, one pillow, flowers and the right curtain; finer textile and floral details are simplified.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
